events.title: The seventh kiln-pit dug at Morn
events.body: A household of the Seann-Dhaoine finishes a seventh stone-lined smoking pit above the shingle at Morn, each fed by a short turf-cut flue and kept for smoke and not flame, the first buildings raised on Dia-thìr for a trade rather than a hearth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fish-kilns of Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns at Morn

events.title: The kiln smoke seen from inland
events.body: Herders of the inland hearths mark a grey column standing over the coast on still mornings and take it for a weather of that shore alone, not knowing for some years that it is a fire kept low and smouldering on purpose, day upon day, to dry a catch too great for one winter's eating.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fish-kilns of Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns at Morn

events.title: A kiln is fed with dry peat only
events.body: The keeper of the kilns at Morn keeps a store of dry peat under an overhang of turf for the kiln fires alone, holding that green peat flares where dry peat smokes, and a flare undoes a season's catch.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fish-kilns of Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns at Morn

events.title: The fourth pit drowned in a night's rain
events.body: A gale drives rain sideways off the bay at Morn and puts out the fourth kiln before the keeper's last round; she lets the pit stand cold rather than relight it under a soaked load, and carries the spoiled catch to the gulls at the tideline.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fish-kilns of Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns at Morn

events.title: The ninth kiln set higher against the rain
events.body: The keeper of Morn's kilns digs a ninth pit set higher on the rise than the first seven, its flue longer and angled harder against a driving rain, after a wet night once cost the household a whole pit's catch.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fish-kilns of Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns at Morn

events.title: The keeper teaches the wet-night watch to her niece
events.body: The keeper of the kilns teaches her niece to watch a kiln past the hour she would go to bed on a night of gathering rain, since a fire low enough to smoke is near enough to going out that a hard rain can take it.

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns at Morn

events.title: The first ramp-slab laid at Brenn
events.body: A household of skin-boat builders on the north coast begins laying flat slabs down a shelf of stone at Brenn from above the highest tide to deep water, meaning to draw down a load heavier than any hide boat's frame.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: A ramp-slab relaid twice at Brenn
events.body: Twice a slab of the new ramp at Brenn settles crooked overnight where the ground beneath it runs soft, and is levered up with poles of green oak and reset on stone packed hard by hand and heel, without complaint from the household doing it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: The first ramp at Brenn finished
events.body: The first ramp at Brenn stands finished its whole length, laid true enough that a loaded sledge runs it without a check, some years before the household raises anything heavier upon it than the skin boats they had always built.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: A dog lies across the finished ramp
events.body: A dog of the Brenn household lies full length on the finished ramp on warm days, and the household steps over it on the way down to the water rather than move it.

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: The first plank-built hull framed at Brenn
events.body: The household at Brenn frames the first hull of planks pegged and caulked over a timber frame, a make no shore of Dia-thìr had built before, and raises it on rollers along the finished ramp to wait on the tide.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn
events.body: Long ramps of flat stone are laid down into the water at Seann Bhrenn, wide enough for hulls greater than any hide boat. Of the hulls nothing is left, nor any telling of where they went.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first ramp-slab laid at Brenn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A ramp-slab relaid twice at Brenn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first ramp at Brenn finished

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first plank-built hull framed at Brenn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first hull launched down the ramps

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first hull goes out past the last shelf

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: A sail seen small from the height above Brenn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A second ramp begun at Brenn

events.title: The first hull launched down the ramps
events.body: The household of Brenn walks its first plank-built hull down the finished ramp on rollers and lets it take the water at the height of the tide; it floats low and steady, and hands already aboard it work it out past the last stone shelf into open water.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: The first hull goes out past the last shelf
events.body: The hull launched from Brenn is worked out past the last shelf of stone into open water, and of where it went, or what it was built to reach, nothing is told.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: A sail seen small from the height above Brenn
events.body: A watcher on high ground along the coast near Brenn marks a dark sail standing out against the grey water and shrinking until it cannot be told from the sea it stands on, then turns back to the day's work once there is nothing left to watch.

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: IV. Of the Shore Grown Bold

events.title: The first platform driven at Loch chrom
events.body: Oak piles are driven down through the shallows of Loch chrom to firmer ground beneath, and a floor of split timber raised across their tops, joined to the shore by a walk of planks lashed to crossbeams below; whose hands began it, no telling has kept.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lake dwellings of Loch chrom

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses on the Water

events.title: The planks of the lake walks listened to
events.body: A child of the Loch chrom platforms is sent along every plank walk each morning to listen for the sound of a plank gone thin under its light weight before a grown foot finds it the hard way.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lake dwellings of Loch chrom

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses on the Water

events.title: The lake dwellings of Loch chrom
events.body: Platforms on oak piles are raised in the shallows of Loch chrom and joined to the shore by plank walks. Whether the Seann-Dhaoine built them, or some other people of those years, is not known.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first platform driven at Loch chrom

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The planks of the lake walks listened to

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eels first taken from beneath the platforms

links.label: At the same time
links.title: A child carries the first basket the length of the longest walk

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A new pile driven at Loch chrom

events.title: Eels first taken from beneath the platforms
events.body: The households of Loch chrom learn to lower baited traps through gaps left in the plank floors of their platforms, finding more eels gathered in the shade and stillness of the piles than any open bank of the loch had ever drawn to a hand's reach before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The lake dwellings of Loch chrom

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses on the Water

events.title: A child carries the first basket the length of the longest walk
events.body: A child of one household at Loch chrom is trusted, for the first time, to carry a basket of the day's eels the whole length of the longest plank walk alone, watched without a word by an elder who by then counts the crossing an ordinary errand.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: The lake dwellings of Loch chrom

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses on the Water

events.title: A shared meal for a new pile
events.body: The households of the lake platforms count a new oak pile driven and holding as an occasion for a shared meal on the nearest platform once the driving-frame is struck down.

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses on the Water

events.title: A new pile driven at Loch chrom
events.body: Four or five hands together drive a fresh oak pile into the mud of Loch chrom in place of one worked loose by years of current, the heaviest labour that shore's households reckon their own, and mark it, once it holds, with a shared meal on the platform.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The lake dwellings of Loch chrom

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: III. Of the Houses on the Water

events.title: A second ramp begun at Brenn
events.body: The household at Brenn lays a second ramp beside the first, wider and longer, and launches hulls from it in the years after the way any trade repeats what it has once learned, though none of those hulls draws the telling's eye as the first one did.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The slipways of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Kilns, the Ramps and the Houses on the Water
told_in.section: II. Of the Ramps at Brenn

events.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn
events.body: A whale strands below the southern Seann Dunn, and its ribs are raised for the frames of three round houses roofed with turf. The ribs are set up again in new houses at least twice before they rot.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A whale strands below the southern Dunn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The whale cut and shared along the shore

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The whale's ribs driven upright for house frames

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Whale oil burned through two winters

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first rib found cracked through

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The whale-rib houses raised a second time

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A child turns up the buried foot of the first rib

events.title: A whale strands below the southern Dunn
events.body: A whale comes ashore in an autumn gale below the southern Dunn, stranded beyond the tide's reach. It lives through a day and a night before its breathing stops, watched from a careful distance by the household nearest the shingle who first heard the surf change its voice.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: The whale cut and shared along the shore
events.body: Word of the stranding carries both ways along the shore, and households beyond the one that found it come down to Dunn to help with the cutting. The meat is salted and smoked, the blubber rendered in clay-lined pits, and no household that helped goes home with an empty basket.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: The whale's ribs driven upright for house frames
events.body: Once the meat and the blubber are taken, the whale's bared ribs are driven upright in the turf above the shingle and lashed together at the crown. Three round houses stand roofed in turf by the year's end, taller and wider than any frame of bent branch the shore had raised before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: Whale oil burned through two winters
events.body: The oil rendered from the whale at the southern Dunn is kept in bladders and clay pots and burned in stone lamps through two winters at least, by more hearths than the one that first heard the surf change.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: The first rib found cracked through
events.body: A rib bearing the heaviest weight of turf is found cracked through in its fifth winter, salt and rain having told on the bone faster than they tell on green wood. It is shored with a driven stake lashed alongside it rather than taken down before the roof can fall.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: The whale-rib houses raised a second time
events.body: The original ribs having failed past shoring, the three houses at Dunn are raised again, this time on bone from a second, smaller stranding that had come ashore some way along the same stretch in the years between, cut by a household with no thought then of building.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: A child turns up the buried foot of the first rib
events.body: Digging in ground long since grown thick with turf, a child of the household turns up a length of bone gone soft and dark with years, and cannot say what it is until an elder names it: the foot of a rib from the first whale-rib house, sunk and near forgotten.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell
events.body: At the eastern Seann Vell the Seann-Dhaoine build round houses of dry stone, each with a hearth sunk in the middle of the floor and a drain running out under the wall. Fourteen house-rings are counted there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eastern Vell's first dry-stone round house

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A hearth sunk below the sunk floor at eastern Vell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first drain cut beneath a wall at eastern Vell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Drains cut under standing walls at Vell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fourteenth house finished at eastern Vell

events.title: A third raising on bone carried from the west
events.body: The rib houses at the southern Dunn are raised a third time on bone carried along the shore from a whale cut further west, word of usable ribs travelling faster by then than word of strandings once did.

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: I. Of the Whale-Ribs at Dunn

events.title: The eastern Vell's first dry-stone round house
events.body: On ground thick with loose slabs above the eastern Vell, a household raises the first of what will become fourteen round houses, dry stone laid without mortar, each course fitted and refitted until it holds by its own weight alone, roofed at last by corbelled slabs closed with turf.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: II. Of the Round Houses of the Eastern Vell

events.title: A hearth sunk below the sunk floor at eastern Vell
events.body: A household of the eastern Vell cuts its hearth-pit deeper than the sunk floor around it and lines it with stone set on edge, keeping the fire below any draught the door might let in, and letting the smoke find its own way out past the corbelled roof's crown.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: II. Of the Round Houses of the Eastern Vell

events.title: The first drain cut beneath a wall at eastern Vell
events.body: A household whose floor stands wetter than its neighbours' through a wet winter takes up its own floor the following dry season and cuts a stone-lined channel under the wall to carry the water clear. Other households of the cluster, watching, take up their own floors in turn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: II. Of the Round Houses of the Eastern Vell

events.title: Drains cut under standing walls at Vell
events.body: Households of the eastern Vell whose houses were built without a drain take up their floors in a dry season and cut the channel in under walls already standing, having watched their neighbours' floors stand drier.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: II. Of the Round Houses of the Eastern Vell

events.title: The fourteenth house finished at eastern Vell
events.body: The last of the fourteen round houses stands finished on the eastern Vell's cleared ground, doors facing every way the ground allows, and every house of the cluster by now given its own dry outfall beneath the wall, a drier floor than the cluster's first years knew.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: II. Of the Round Houses of the Eastern Vell

events.title: A hollow-walled tower begun at the north-western Skell
events.body: A household of the north-western Skell, settled where the ground runs out to open water on three sides, begins a round tower of two dry-stone faces built together, a stair let into the gap between them, climbing the wall's own thickness rather than crossing any open floor.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: III. Of the Tower at the North-Western Skell

events.title: A winter storm throws down the unfinished outer face
events.body: With the tower a third of its final height, a winter storm throws down the outer face of the stair while the inner holds. The household clears the fallen stone from the gap and sets the cross-stones binding the two faces closer together through the whole climb of what remains to be built.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: III. Of the Tower at the North-Western Skell

events.title: The tower at the north-western Seann Skell
events.body: At the least of the Seann Skell places, on the north-west coast, a single round tower of dry stone is raised, hollow-walled, with a stair in the thickness of the wall. It looks out over the water where the Sea-Watcher is afterwards seen.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A hollow-walled tower begun at the north-western Skell

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A winter storm throws down the unfinished outer face

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first night at the tower's crown

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A fire lit on the parapet turns a boat from the rocks

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The stair walked after every storm

events.title: The first night at the tower's crown
events.body: With the stair whole and the parapet laid, a household of the north-western Skell climbs to the tower's open crown by clear starlight and sees more of the sea at once than any of that shore had seen from any roof or headland before it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: III. Of the Tower at the North-Western Skell

events.title: A fire lit on the parapet turns a boat from the rocks
events.body: In hard weather, a boat not of that shore is seen from the tower's crown standing in blind toward the rocks below. A fire lit on the parapet shows its crew the coast they are running for in time to bear off from the worst of it before the light fails.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: III. Of the Tower at the North-Western Skell

events.title: The stair walked after every storm
events.body: The household of the north-western Skell walks the tower stair from foot to crown after every storm, feeling along both faces for any stone gone slack in its bed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: III. Of the Tower at the North-Western Skell

events.title: Stone huts built in the dune's lee at Toll
events.body: A household of Toll builds a row of low stone huts against the slope of a dune tall enough to break the worst of the sea wind before it reaches a wall, turf-roofed and set close, the sand that blows loose in an ordinary gale cleared each morning as an ordinary chore.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The huts of the northern Seann Toll

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: IV. Of the Huts at Toll and the Sand

events.title: A wind rises off the sea that does not settle
events.body: A wind rises off the sea and holds through a full day and into a second, driving sand off the dune's whole face until the air itself thickens to the colour and near the weight of the ground it carries, and sand mounts against the huts faster than hands can clear it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The huts of the northern Seann Toll

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: IV. Of the Huts at Toll and the Sand

events.title: The household of Toll leaves the buried huts
events.body: Before the storm's second night closes on them, the household carries what it can and goes inland to higher ground, none of them lost or badly hurt in the leaving. The dune moves forward the width of the huts and beyond, and the row is not seen again above the sand.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The huts of the northern Seann Toll

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: IV. Of the Huts at Toll and the Sand

events.title: The huts of the northern Seann Toll
events.body: At Seann Toll on the north coast a cluster of stone huts is built in the lee of a dune. The dune afterwards buries them whole, and the sand keeps them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Stone huts built in the dune's lee at Toll

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A wind rises off the sea that does not settle

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The household of Toll leaves the buried huts

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dune moves the width of the huts

links.label: Leads to
links.title: New walls raised inland from the buried row

events.title: The dune moves the width of the huts
events.body: When the wind falls on the third day the dune at the northern Toll stands forward the whole width of the huts and beyond, a slope of new pale sand over ground where doors opened two days before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The huts of the northern Seann Toll

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: IV. Of the Huts at Toll and the Sand

events.title: New walls raised inland from the buried row
events.body: After digging finds the buried huts still whole but past any hope of clearing, the household of Toll gives up the digging and raises new walls further inland, on ground it judges, by the coast's own long habit of wind and sand, unlikely to be claimed again in its own lifetime.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The huts of the northern Seann Toll

told_in.book: Of the Whale, the Round Houses and the Tower
told_in.section: IV. Of the Huts at Toll and the Sand

events.title: The eastern Seann Bhral
events.body: At the Seann Bhral of the south-east coast the Seann-Dhaoine keep a landing and a line of fish-kilns like those of Seann Mhorn. The two places lie within a day's rowing of each other.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The middle kiln judged by smell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The eastern Bral kilns kept alight in relay

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A girl reads the smoke at the eastern kilns

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dried fish given back for a stranded beast's oil

events.title: Gormal takes up Poit an Teine
events.body: Past thirty and past the birth of the one daughter who lived, Gormal takes up Poit an Teine and the leather bag of the line's an gual dathach from an aunt with no living daughter of her own, having already buried a father, an aunt and two of her own age who died saying the sky-coal would never light.

events.title: The middle kiln judged by smell
events.body: The woman who minds the middle kiln at the eastern Bral judges the smoke by its smell at first light and dusk and the fish by the give of the flesh under one finger, and teaches both by standing a child at her elbow.

events.title: Gormal's rule that the recital be kept
events.body: Gormal rules that the fathers' names and Tòimhseachan a' Choimhdich after them be said standing every dark-of-the-year night whether any of the gathered kin care to hear it or not, holding that a recital kept only while it is believed is not kept at all.

events.title: Gormal learns the fathers' names at nine
events.body: Gormal stands the fathers' names over to the aunt who keeps Poit an Teine every evening of a whole winter until not a name comes out of its place, and asks, the first time she hears Tòimhseachan a' Choimhdich whole, why no one has tried from higher ground.

events.title: Three good harvests on the eastern slopes
events.body: Word climbs to the high valleys of a third good harvest running on the farms of the eastern slopes, and the branch of the kin already drifting down toward that lower ground begins drifting faster, households following one another rather than waiting their own turn to go.

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: II. Of Gormal and the Kin That Went Down

events.title: The branch leaves with no coal of the vein
events.body: The last households of the eastern branch load their gear onto ox-sledges and go down from the high valleys for good, carrying a coal from their own daily fire and not one splinter of the mason's vein, the first households of the line ever to leave it empty-handed.

events.title: Gormal names three hills for the sky
events.body: At the recital after the branch's leaving, Gormal argues that the sky, like the sea, should be tried from the ground nearest it, and names three hills of her own judging, one south of the black well, one west toward Achadh dhìreach and a bare shoulder of moor she herself favours, though the kin cannot agree which of the three, or any other, truly stands highest.

events.title: Gormal meets the branch at the sledges
events.body: Gormal walks out to the yard where the last of the going branch lash their sledges and tells them that no household has gone from the line empty of the vein before; she does not ask them to stay.

events.title: The eastern Bral kilns kept alight in relay
events.body: At the eastern landing three fish-kilns are kept fed at any time while three stand cold and swept, a household's whole catch never dried on the same night lest a failed wind leave it with nothing, the kilns built and worked in the same way as the sister kilns a day's rowing to the south.

links.title: The eastern Seann Bhral

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns in the East

events.title: A girl reads the smoke at the eastern kilns
events.body: A granddaughter of the woman who minds the middle kiln at the eastern landing notices, before anyone older has remarked it, that the smoke of that kiln runs paler than its neighbours in some seasons though the fire beneath is fed no differently, and is told only that the smoke says what the smoke says.

links.title: The eastern Seann Bhral

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns in the East

events.title: Dried fish given back for a stranded beast's oil
events.body: When a beast comes ashore dead below the southern kilns, the eastern landing sends back a share of its own dried fish by the same boat that brought the word, the giving between the two places running both ways over the years without either side keeping any closer account of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The eastern Seann Bhral

told_in.section: I. Of the Kilns in the East

events.title: Sìomha softens the recital for her own children
events.body: Gormal's daughter Sìomha, unable to move her mother from the fixed words, begins saying the fathers' names and Tòimhseachan a' Choimhdich to her own children in gentler terms at her own hearth, without ever once letting the recital itself lapse.

events.title: The southern oyster mound stands taller than any household's reach
events.body: Along the southern headland the pile of raked and eaten oyster shell, built up by generations of the same households, comes to stand higher at its oldest end than a tall man can reach with his arm above his head, whiter at the crown where gulls have picked it clean.

links.title: The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: III. Of the Oyster Beds in the South

events.title: Gormal adds her own words at her last recital
events.body: At the last recital she stands for, Gormal adds to the fixed words that the line has not yet thrown from the one hill that matters, and that whoever finds it will do the line more good in an afternoon than the branch in ten generations.

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: II. Of Gormal and the Kin That Went Down

events.title: A worn rake laid on the southern mound
events.body: A woman of the southern shore, famed along that coast for the truest oyster-rake anyone there remembers, dies leaving it to her strongest-armed granddaughter; when it wears past mending in its turn it is laid on the mound itself rather than burned or given back to the sea, by a custom the shore explains to no outsider.

links.title: The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: III. Of the Oyster Beds in the South

events.title: Gormal's last recital
events.body: On the last dark-of-the-year night of her life Gormal says Tòimhseachan a' Choimhdich standing as she has said it every year of her keeping, and adds, unfixed in the words, that whoever first agrees which hill stands highest will do the line more good than the branch that went down to the farms did it in ten generations of easier digging.

told_in.section: II. Of Gormal and the Kin That Went Down

events.title: Gormal dies
events.body: Gormal dies that winter in the house she kept Poit an Teine in her whole life, her daughter Sìomha and a granddaughter at her bedside, the six dark coals laid out on the blanket at her own asking; the bag and the unanswered question pass to hands that had heard her say both enough times to say them back the same way.

told_in.section: II. Of Gormal and the Kin That Went Down

events.title: The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn
events.body: At the second Seann Mhorn, on the southern coast, oyster, whelk and cockle shell is heaped over a whole headland, and there is little else. The oysters of its lowest layers are larger than any taken there since.

events.title: The oldest shells of the southern mound run large
events.body: The raking households of the southern Morn find that the oysters of the lowest layers of their mound are broader by half than any taken from the same water in living memory, and do not trouble over why.

events.title: A third ramp begun at the second Brenn
events.body: Far to the north-east a household that first rolled boulders into its own river's current and walked hulls down over them, in the same way as a household on a river far to the west that bears the same name, begins a third ramp beside the first two, having hulls enough to want more room than two ramps give it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The twin landings of Seann Bhrenn

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Landing

events.title: The twin landings of Seann Bhrenn
events.body: A second Seann Bhrenn, far to the north-east of the first, has the same long ramps into the water. Whether the two were of one people, or only the name was carried, is not known.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A third ramp begun at the second Brenn

events.title: A boy stands before the twin ramps of Brenn
events.body: Sent one autumn morning to carry word along the bank that the tide has turned, a boy of the north-eastern Brenn household stands a long while looking at the two, then three, pale ramps running into the current before running his errand, and says nothing after of what he stood looking at.

told_in.book: Of the Lean Years of the Line
told_in.section: IV. Of the Second Landing

events.title: Mathan born
events.body: A second son is born to the household of Clann a' Chlachair at Tobar dhìreach, three years before his brother Fearghas, a long-legged child who from the first is surer on wet rock than any of the kin his own age.

links.label: Same person

told_in.book: Of Fearghas on the Height
told_in.section: I. Of the Two Brothers and the Three Hills

events.title: Fearghas born
events.body: Fearghas is born at Tobar dhìreach into Clann a' Chlachair, growing up on Gormal's unsettled riddle of the three hills as every child of the line grows up on it, turning the six dark coals over in his own hands before he is old enough to feel either the wonder or the doubt older mouths bring to the same handling.

told_in.book: Of Fearghas on the Height
told_in.section: I. Of the Two Brothers and the Three Hills

events.title: Mathan names the fault in Gormal's three hills
events.body: Mathan says aloud, to his brother, what each of them has been turning over apart: that Gormal named her three hills from where she stood and never climbed higher than her own doorstep to judge between them, and that the line has legs enough to settle the question by walking rather than by arguing at the hearth.

events.title: The brothers stand on the first of Gormal's three hills
events.body: Fearghas and Mathan climb the hill south of the black well, the nearest of the three heights Gormal once named, and standing on its crown cannot agree between them whether the shoulder of moor she had favoured stands higher still, learning only that no one of the three can be judged fairly against the others without climbing each in turn.

events.title: A herder of the southern moor points beyond the known ground
events.body: An old herder driving his flock along a saddle of moor tells the two brothers of a further shoulder his own father swore stood higher than anything nearer the valleys, though the father himself never went to prove it, and sends them on with nothing but the names of a burn and a stand of thorn to steer by.

events.title: Two summers of walking ridges
events.body: Fearghas and Mathan walk south in the fair months and come back before the hard ones, each season a little further, climbing hills that looked from a distance like the last word and proved to have a taller neighbour behind them.

events.title: A climb lost to rain
events.body: Fearghas and Mathan climb the shoulder the herder's father had sworn by and stand on it in a driving rain that shows them nothing of the ground beyond, coming down soaked and short-tempered with each other over whether the wetting had been worth it.

told_in.section: I. Of the Two Brothers and the Three Hills

events.title: The true height is sighted
events.body: In clearer weather three summers into their walking, Fearghas and Mathan come out from behind a shoulder of bare rock and see, standing above every other height in every direction, a grey summit with cloud dragging along its crown, and know without needing to say it that the walking is nearly done.

events.title: The brothers set out for the height
events.body: Carrying the six dark coals wrapped against the wet in the leather bag, Fearghas and Mathan climb through the last night of summer toward the summit that stands clear over the whole island, sleeping little for the wind and going up with the first grey of morning.

events.title: The snowflake coal takes fire in the air
events.body: Fearghas of the Mason's line climbs to the highest ground of the island, above where Muileann gheal now stands, and lets the six unlit coals fall from the top. The coal flecked with white stars takes fire as it falls and burns white in the air; the others strike the stones cold. The summit is called after the kindred: Binnean a' Chlachair, the Mason's Point.

events.body: Before the brothers leave the summit where gual sneachda has just taken fire in the falling air, Mathan sets one loose stone from the crown atop another, a small cairn no higher than a hand, and says nothing over it that needs saying.

events.title: The telling reaches every hearth within a day's walk
events.body: By the morning after Fearghas and Mathan tell it standing at Tobar dhìreach, with the four cold coals laid out on a cloth for any hand to turn over, word of the lighting on the height has gone out to every household within a day's walk, carried by whoever heard it first and could not keep from carrying it further.

events.body: After the snowflake takes fire, Fearghas lets the sixth coal fall from the summit for the sake of the telling, and it strikes the stones as cold as the four before it.

events.body: Fearghas and Mathan climb down to the white-burning coal and leave it where it lies, judging that it has found its own place as surely as the gold found the sea.

events.title: The first stone left by a stranger's hand
events.body: A herder of the high valleys, passing within sight of the grey summit for the first time since the telling went out, climbs to Mathan's small cairn and lays a stone of his own beside it, the first stone set there by a hand not of Clann a' Chlachair, beginning a custom that outlives everyone then living.

events.title: Herders' stones heap on the summit
events.body: Within a lifetime the little cairn Mathan began on the summit of Binnean a' Chlachair is a heap of stones a man can see from some way off, each laid by a passing herder and none of them saying why.

events.title: Fearghas climbs the height with his son
events.body: Fearghas, his hair gone grey, climbs the height a second time with his own son grown old enough for the way, and shows him the white fire still burning steady among the cold stones below the summit exactly as he had first seen it catch, unchanged in every particular.

events.title: Mathan dies
events.body: Mathan dies of a fever that comes on him in a wet spring and will not break, five and fifty years old, and is buried at Tobar dhìreach with the first cairn stone he ever set on the height closed in one hand at his own asking, having given the height, as he put it himself, three summers of his legs and his best notion.

events.title: Fearghas's last climb
events.body: An old man now, three days each way instead of two, Fearghas climbs to the height a last time alone and finds the white coal burning exactly as he left it every time before, and leaves a stone of his own on the crown before coming down for good.

events.title: Fearghas dies
events.body: Fearghas dies at Tobar dhìreach in his sixty-second year, sure to the last of his own two feet on the height he had proved, and is buried within sight of Leac na Fèithe that covers the mason's vein as every keeper and finder of the line is buried before him.

events.body: At the recital said over Fearghas's grave, the reciter gives his name for the first time after his father's in the fixed words of the fathers of the line, telling how he climbed to the top of the island and let the six coals fall, and how the snowflake took fire in the empty air and gave the summit its name.

events.title: The long house at Tarr set against the cliff
events.body: A household of the north-eastern Tarr builds a single long house into a cleft of the cliff, the living rock its own back wall, needing to raise stone only where the cliff itself did not already stand higher than any wall the household could have built.

told_in.section: I. Of the Long House at Tarr

events.title: The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east
events.body: At the Seann Tarr of the north-eastern headlands a single long house is built into a cleft of the cliff, with the living rock for its back wall. The rock behind the hearth is black with soot to the height of a man.

events.title: The hearth blackens the rock behind it
events.body: Years of the same fire kept against the same face of the cliff blacken the stone above the hearth to the height of a tall man standing, a stain the household never scrubs and never troubles to explain, holding a blackened rock over a hearth no stranger a thing than a blackened pot.

told_in.section: I. Of the Long House at Tarr

events.title: The hard winter at Tarr
events.body: A wind out of the north holds the better part of two months without turning, and the household at Tarr lives on dried stores and shellfish taken between gales, burning at the last the timbers of a spare boat-frame kept against just such a want rather than let the hearth go cold.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east

told_in.section: I. Of the Long House at Tarr

events.title: The calm morning after the hard winter
events.body: The wind drops in a single night and swings out of the north at last; the household goes down to the shingle before light to stand out of the wind, and finds a run of small fish thick enough in the shallows to be taken by hand.

events.title: The four houses raised at the Vell on the Abhainn bheag
events.body: A short way above the river's mouth in the north-east, four houses and a boat-shed are raised on ground cut level into the steep bank; no dwelling of the shore-folk on the island is known to stand further to the north-east than this small place.

told_in.section: II. Of the Vell on the Abhainn Bheag

events.title: A girl measures her growing by the soot
events.body: A child of the cliff-house at Tarr stands with her back to the soot-stain on the rock above the hearth each midwinter to see how far up it her crown reaches, until the year she stands as tall as the stain.

told_in.section: I. Of the Long House at Tarr

events.title: A flat-bottomed hull built for the river
events.body: The Vell's boat-shed is built to keep a hull dry between one season's use and the next; the household raises a boat flat enough in the bottom to be poled past the first rapids in a dry season, and takes it further upriver than any of the four households has gone on foot.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The north-eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: II. Of the Vell on the Abhainn Bheag

events.title: A second small fire lit at the door in the dark months
events.body: The household of the Tarr cliff-house keeps a second small fire lit just inside the door on the darkest days, more for its light than its warmth, the cliff keeping the sun from the doorway through the shortest months.

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: I. Of the Long House at Tarr

events.title: A spring flood reaches the boat-shed
events.body: Snow melting fast off the central massif sends the Abhainn bheag over its bank far enough to reach the boat-shed's lower course; the household clears the silted floor by the basket-load and raises the shed a course higher on its uphill side.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The north-eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: II. Of the Vell on the Abhainn Bheag

events.title: A girl of the river Vell stops at the river's mouth
events.body: A woman grown up at the Vell on the Abhainn bheag stands at the river's mouth one evening looking at the open sea and goes no further, holding that a river's own child has no business beyond its mouth.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The north-eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: II. Of the Vell on the Abhainn Bheag

events.title: Dried fish carried south to kin without a river
events.body: The Vell on the Abhainn bheag spares a share of its eel and salmon catch, smoked over slow fires, to kin two days' walk to the south who keep no river of their own; a household comes up once in a lean year with little to trade and goes home with more than it brought.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The north-eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: II. Of the Vell on the Abhainn Bheag

events.title: The north-eastern Seann Vell
events.body: The Seann Vell on the Abhainn bheag, a short way above its mouth in the north-east, is a small place of four houses and a boat-shed. No Seann-Dhaoine dwelling on the main island is known further to the north-east.

links.title: The four houses raised at the Vell on the Abhainn bheag

links.title: The eel-trap pattern taught to two children

events.title: The eel-trap pattern taught to two children
events.body: An old woman of the Vell's youngest household teaches the willow-trap pattern she learned as a girl to a boy and a girl of the place, holding that a pattern known in only one pair of hands is one bad season from being lost to the whole Vell.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The north-eastern Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: II. Of the Vell on the Abhainn Bheag

events.title: The second Skell begins its own curved mole
events.body: A household of a northern Skell some way along the coast from the first breakwater takes up the same work for its own water, laying stone out from a low headland in the same curve, carried down from a scree behind the shore rather than quarried fresh.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The northern Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: III. Of the Second Mole at Skell

events.title: A swell breaks over the unfinished mole and moves nothing
events.body: A hard swell out of the north-west runs white over the second Skell's unfinished curve for two days; when it drops every stone is found still set where it was laid, moved a hand's width here and there but nowhere thrown clear.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The northern Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: III. Of the Second Mole at Skell

events.title: Each stone of the curved mole laid dry first
events.body: The household building the second mole at the northern Skell lays each new stone dry against the course already set, working it back and forth until it sits without rocking, and only then sets it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The northern Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: III. Of the Second Mole at Skell

events.title: The northern Seann Skell
events.body: At the Seann Skell below the later Ros gheal, on the north coast, the Seann-Dhaoine lay a second breakwater, shorter than the southern one and curved against the swell of the open sea. The two moles are built the same way, stone by stone.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The second Skell begins its own curved mole

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A swell breaks over the unfinished mole and moves nothing

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Each stone of the curved mole laid dry first

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The curved mole at the second Skell finished

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A traveller from the second Skell sees the first mole

events.title: The curved mole at the second Skell finished
events.body: The second Skell's breakwater is carried out as far as the household judges worth the sheltering; a boat brought in behind the finished curve on a hard-weather day rides easier at its mooring than any boat of that shore had ridden before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The northern Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: III. Of the Second Mole at Skell

events.title: A traveller from the second Skell sees the first mole
events.body: A man of the second Skell, grown from the boy who watched his own household's curve laid, comes within sight of the first mole on a journey south and finds the stone laid the same way, curve for curve, though no household of either shore had ever seen the other's work before it was finished.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The northern Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: III. Of the Second Mole at Skell

events.title: The first clay-lined pit dug in the western dune
events.body: A woman of the western Vell digs and clay-lines the first of a line of storage pits cut into the dune's slope, closed with a heavy slab; households after her keep her spacing between pits without troubling to test her reasoning for themselves.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The western Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: IV. Of the Pits in the Western Dune

events.title: A younger household cuts clay out of turn
events.body: A household new to the western dune cuts a clay bank two others had agreed to leave fallow a season; once the disagreement reaches her, the woman who keeps the unwritten turn among the banks settles it, and the younger household gives over a full pit's worth of its own dried catch.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The western Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: IV. Of the Pits in the Western Dune

events.title: The pits of the western dune spaced a body's length apart
events.body: The woman who dug the first store-pit in the western dune at Vell sets her later pits a full body's length apart, holding that a pit dug too near another draws damp, and the households after her keep the spacing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The western Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: IV. Of the Pits in the Western Dune

events.title: The western Seann Vell
events.body: At the Seann Vell of the west coast the Seann-Dhaoine dig a line of storage pits into the dune, lined with clay and lidded with slabs. Some held fish bones still when they were opened.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The first clay-lined pit dug in the western dune

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A younger household cuts clay out of turn

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The pits of the western dune spaced a body's length apart

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fish bones found in a sealed pit

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Doors of the western shore turn from the sea

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last pit of the season sealed for winter

events.title: Fish bones found in a sealed pit
events.body: A pit left sealed longer than a season gives back fish bones picked clean and gone soft with damp that found its way past the clay; the households learn to trust a pit's seal less far into a second year and to empty a store before the season turns.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The western Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: IV. Of the Pits in the Western Dune

events.title: Doors of the western shore turn from the sea
events.body: Without any of its own tellings naming a reason, household after household of the western shore sets its door and its hearth a little more toward the dune at its back than toward the water in front, a threshold that had always opened straight onto the beach coming to open sideways from it instead.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The western Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: IV. Of the Pits in the Western Dune

events.title: The last pit of the season sealed for winter
events.body: The western dune's last pit of the year is dug, lined and lidded before the first hard frost, the sand banked back over its edges as every pit before it had been closed, the shore settling into a waiting none of its tellings say the whole of.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The western Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Cliff-House and the Curved Mole
told_in.section: IV. Of the Pits in the Western Dune

events.title: The spur first climbed and looked from
events.body: Two sons of a shore household climb the spur above the southern lowland to look, and come back saying a man standing on its crown can see the whole lowland below him and any thing that moves across it long before it reaches the coast.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised
events.body: On a spur above the ground where Cathair mhòr now stands, the Seann-Dhaoine build the walled outpost afterwards called Làrach an Dùin-fhaire. Its stones are dressed on the outer face only, and its single gate looks inland, away from the sea.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The spur first climbed and looked from

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's wall dressed on its outer face only

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The inner face of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire left rough

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's gate hung

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cattle first driven up the spur

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The gate argued before the lintel

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The false watch on the lowland

events.title: The three rings begun on the height
events.body: On a height near the south-eastern coast a crew begins the outer of three ringed walls under a woman said to read the ground before a stone is laid, a work on a scale no household of that coast has raised to before.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Làrach an Dùin raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's wall dressed on its outer face only
events.body: The mason who sets Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's first course dresses its stone smooth only where an enemy's eye might run along it, leaving the inner face raw, so that the wall stands smooth without and rough within through every season it is kept.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: The inner face of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire left rough
events.body: The woman who sets the first course of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire wall dresses the stones on the outer face only, saying a wall need be smooth where an enemy's eye runs looking for a hold, and rough where a friend's hand rests going up the inner steps.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's gate hung
events.body: A heavy oaken gate is hung on a socketed post at Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, its single doorway facing inland away from the sea, and swings shut of its own weight for the first time to the doubt of an old fisherman who mistrusts a door built facing from the water.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: Cattle first driven up the spur
events.body: Beasts used to level shore grazing are coaxed up the spur's steep ground for the first time, balking at the new gate, and settle within the wall to its thin grass within a few days of the climb.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: The gate argued before the lintel
events.body: An old fisherman argues that a gate facing away from the water is a gate built by people who have forgotten what the water was to them; the mason answers that whatever a gate here must watch for will not come rowing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: A watcher learns to prefer the quiet
events.body: A woman who keeps Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's first winter watch longer than anyone of her household says afterward that the quiet of the spur had a weight unlike any quiet of the shore, and that she grew almost to prefer it.

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: The false watch on the lowland
events.body: A boy of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raises the whole watch at dusk over shapes crossing the lowland from the west, taken for deer moving too evenly together; nothing is found by first light, and Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's watch is never again left to one pair of eyes.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: I. Of the Wall on the Spur

events.title: The cistern cut into the bedrock
events.body: At the height's crown a basin is hollowed from the bedrock by heated stone cracked loose and cooled with water, a labour of two seasons that blisters more hands than the rest of the rings together.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Làrach an Dùin raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: The one who reads the ground stands over the cistern
events.body: The woman who reads the ground for the three rings says the cistern must go deep enough to hold water through a summer no rain falls in, though no one living has seen such a summer.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Làrach an Dùin raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: Làrach an Dùin raised
events.body: A greater work is raised on the height near Ceann mhin: three rings of wall, a cistern cut into the bedrock, and room within, as it was later reckoned, for four hundred people and their beasts. Whether the builders of the outpost built this also has never been settled.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The three rings begun on the height

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The cistern cut into the bedrock

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The one who reads the ground stands over the cistern

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The cistern first full

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cattle first driven inside the three rings

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The death of the woman who read the ground

events.title: The cistern first full
events.body: The cistern fills for the first time from a spring the digging uncovers, and a child let down on a rope draws up the first measure, which the woman who read the ground tastes and says tastes of stone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: Cattle first driven inside the three rings
events.body: Beasts are driven up the steeper climb into the three rings for the first time, more lost to loose scree on the way than the spur's own herders ever lost, and a woman who loses two of her own says the rings charge dear for what they let in.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: The wind within the rings
events.body: A household that moves up from the shore to one of the first houses within the innermost ring finds the wind there, filtered through three walls, gentler than any wind it knew at the water's edge.

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: The trodden way between the heights first paved
events.body: A household along the worst stretch of the path between the spur and the height lays flat stones to keep its own feet dry, with no thought yet of any greater road, and others add paving of their own beside it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The kerbed way between the forts

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: III. Of the Kerbed Way

events.title: The death of the woman who read the ground
events.body: The woman who has read the ground for the three rings since the first course dies within the innermost ring at a great age and is buried there at her own asking, under a stretch of wall she named the soundest of her life.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Dùin raised

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: II. Of the Cistern and the Three Rings

events.title: The kerbed way between the forts
events.body: A kerbed track, a cart's width and paved with flat slabs, is laid through the ground near Àth fhionn toward both strongholds. It is the only road the Seann-Dhaoine are known to have made away from the shore.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The trodden way between the heights first paved

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The kerbing of the way spreads

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The kerbed way paved household by household

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first cart driven the whole way

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last slab of the kerbed way laid

events.title: The kerbing of the way spreads
events.body: Upright stones set along the paving's edges hold it firm through a wet winter better than the unkerbed stretches beside it, and the practice spreads along the whole track within a few more seasons.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The kerbed way between the forts

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: III. Of the Kerbed Way

events.title: The kerbed way paved household by household
events.body: The track between Làrach an Dùin-fhaire and the rings is paved stretch by stretch by the households nearest each stretch, pale stone and dark, broad slabs and small fitted stones, no one hand holding the whole plan of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The kerbed way between the forts

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: III. Of the Kerbed Way

events.title: The first cart driven the whole way
events.body: A cart of dressed stone drawn by two yoked oxen crosses the whole kerbed way for the first time without a wheel sinking to the axle, a day's haul where the same load once took the better part of three over open moor.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The kerbed way between the forts

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: III. Of the Kerbed Way

events.title: The last slab of the kerbed way laid
events.body: The final slab of the track is set tilted rather than level on the last steep rise, and the small crew that lays it turns, its work done, to look inland toward the high pale country rather than back toward the sea.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The kerbed way between the forts

told_in.book: Of the Outpost and the Three Rings
told_in.section: III. Of the Kerbed Way

events.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised
events.body: A stepped platform of fitted stone is built in the eastern hills, with an altar block on its top step. The altar is set square to the central mountains. Every later temple on Dia-thìr faces some other way.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first steps of the platform laid

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The great stone dragged up on rollers

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first dawn at the altar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Other households begin to climb

links.title: The last step laid flush with the moor

events.title: The first steps of the platform laid
events.body: A household of the eastern hills begins laying flat stone in steps up the slope below the height, bedding each slab before the next is set above it, the first work of the platform that will in time carry the altar block on its topmost step.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: The great stone dragged up on rollers
events.body: The block meant for the platform's top step is hauled up the finished lower steps on rollers of trimmed timber, the same labour that raised Làrach an Dùin-fhaire wall and Làrach an Dùin rings, and set back from the step's outer edge to be dressed flat.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: The first dawn at the altar
events.body: A household of the southern lowland climbs the finished steps at first light on the shortest morning of the year and stands about the great stone as the sun's light runs along its face toward the mountains it is squared to. No telling records what, if anything, was said.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: Other households begin to climb
events.body: Seeing the first household return year on year to the shortest morning, other families of the eastern hills take up the same climb, until the one gathering at the platform draws more households together than any single one of them could climb the steps alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: The shortest morning climbed in cloud
events.body: In a year when cloud lies thick over the eastern hills through the shortest morning, the households climb the platform steps in the dark and the cold all the same and stand about the great stone the whole hour the light would have taken to cross it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: The last step laid flush with the moor
events.body: The lowest step of the platform is set flush with the level ground, closing the run years after the great stone above it already stood finished, and it is this easiest step, rather than any harder-won one above, that the households nearest it remember longest.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: A carved bird left at the stone's foot
events.body: A woman carries a small carved bird up the platform steps once and sets it at the foot of the great stone, and goes down without it; no second such bird is ever found there.

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: A stranger turned away from the platform
events.body: A stranger up from the southern lowland asks a woman drawing water why the great stone is raised. She answers that a stone older than her grandmother's grandmother needs no explaining to one not born to it, and he does not climb the steps or come again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Làrach an Teampaill raised

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: I. Of the Platform in the Eastern Hills

events.title: The digging begins at the eastern Toll-dubh
events.body: On level moor in the south-east a household begins cutting a well-like shaft straight down through the rock, the work continuing past any depth a well would need and its walls smoothed by hand long after the digging alone would have left them rough.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: The baskets carried off and not returned
events.body: Each evening the broken rock the digging throws off is carried away over the rise at the moor's edge, and no heap of it is ever afterward found anywhere near the shaft's mouth, though no telling says where it was taken.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east
events.body: A shaft is sunk straight down through the rock at the eastern Toll-dubh, its walls tooled smooth as far as a lamp will show. No spoil lies beside it. Whatever was taken out was carried away, or nothing was.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The digging begins at the eastern Toll-dubh

links.title: The baskets carried off and not returned

links.title: A cord lengthened for the lamp

links.title: A young man hurt in the eastern shaft

links.title: The lamp lowered in the eastern shaft

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A stone dropped and heard to fall nowhere

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A stone laid over the shaft at the first frost

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two shafts left open and shunned

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The youth of the south-east asks to go down

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lamp goes small in the eastern shaft

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The youth comes up ash-faced and silent

events.title: A cord lengthened for the lamp
events.body: The plaited cord that lets the lamp down to judge the smoothing of the shaft's walls is lengthened for the third time, the household gathering at the lip each time to watch the lamp go down further than it has gone before and come up still burning.

links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: A young man hurt in the eastern shaft
events.body: Sent down to free a caught basket, a young man of the household comes up with a gash along one forearm that keeps him from the heaviest carrying a season, and returns to the cord the following spring all the same.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: The cord hung inside the door
events.body: The worn lengths of hide cord the eastern shaft was measured with are hung, when renewed, inside the household's door, where another household might hang a net.

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: The lamp lowered in the eastern shaft
events.body: The lamp is let down further than ever before, its light at the bottom showing no more of the walls than a small patch no wider than two hands held apart, the rest standing dark above and below it; the digging is remembered to have stopped near this same evening.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: A stone dropped and heard to fall nowhere
events.body: After the digging stops, a stone let fall from the lip gives back no sound of striking anything below, and the household stands listening far longer than it kept silence for anything else in all the years of that work.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: A stone laid over the shaft at the first frost
events.body: The household of the eastern Toll-dubh lays a flat stone loosely over the shaft's mouth at each year's first hard frost and lifts it after the shortest days, to keep a beast or a careless foot from the lip.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: II. Of the Shaft at the Eastern Toll-dubh

events.title: The digging begins at the western Toll-dubh
events.body: Far across the island, on ground its own people likewise call Toll-dubh, a second household begins a straight, round shaft of the same make as the eastern one, with no telling saying that either household knew of the other's work.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: III. Of the Shaft at the Western Toll-dubh

events.title: A girl asks how deep the shaft will go
events.body: A girl of the western household asks her mother whether the shaft is being dug down to wherever the mountains keep their roots; her mother answers only that the ground keeps its own matters, and that a household does well not to ask them aloud.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: III. Of the Shaft at the Western Toll-dubh

events.title: An old man keeps the lamp trimmed at the western shaft
events.body: A man of the western household, past the heaviest carrying, keeps the lamp trimmed each evening for whoever goes down to judge the smoothing of the western shaft.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: III. Of the Shaft at the Western Toll-dubh

events.title: The lamp left to burn itself out
events.body: The household at the western shaft takes up a habit of setting the lamp, still burning, on a stone by the lip each evening rather than snuffing it, letting it go out on its own, a small custom none of its own tellings gives a reason for keeping.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: III. Of the Shaft at the Western Toll-dubh

events.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west
events.body: A second shaft of the same making is cut at the western Toll-dubh, far across the island from the first. Stones thrown into either are not heard to land.

links.title: The two shafts left open and shunned

events.title: The last stone dropped at the western shaft
events.body: On the evening the western digging is given over, the youngest of the household lets a stone fall and counts under his breath until he judges it must have struck bottom; when no sound comes, he looks to the faces around him rather than down the shaft.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west

told_in.book: Of the Altar and the Shafts
told_in.section: III. Of the Shaft at the Western Toll-dubh

events.title: The two shafts left open and shunned
events.body: Both shafts stand unfilled and uncovered at the century's turn, and travellers of either coast come to walk wide of their mouths, letting a dropped stone go down into a silence no household troubles any longer to break by listening after it.

events.title: Bran born to the north-west shore
events.body: Bran is born to a fishing hearth of the north-west shore, kin who keep Aithris a' Chruthachaidh as every hill hearth does but hear its westward part first, the part that names Tìr nan Òg, Magh Meall and Taigh Dhuinn across the open sea.

links.title: The First Canoe

links.title: Bran stands at the tideline at dusk

told_in.book: Of the Steersman
told_in.section: I. Of the Word of the West

events.title: Bran stands at the tideline at dusk
events.body: Bran, near ten, is found by his mother at the tideline deep into the dark, looking at the place where it stops being water and starts being something else.

links.label: Same person
links.title: Bran born to the north-west shore

links.label: Same person

told_in.book: Of the Steersman
told_in.section: I. Of the Word of the West

events.title: The best boatman of that coast
events.body: Grown to a man, Bran is known the length of the north-west shore as the surest hand with a swell and a stitching-needle alike, mending hulls that no other boatman's seams will hold and reading weather other men cannot.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The First Canoe

told_in.book: Of the Steersman
told_in.section: I. Of the Word of the West

events.title: Bran mends every boat on the shore
events.body: Neighbours bring Bran their boats from half a day's walk along the coast because his stitches hold where other men's let the sea in, and he asks no payment but a share of what the mended boat brings home.

links.label: Same person
links.title: The best boatman of that coast
